body: [Home](https://schwabnetwork.com)[Articles](https://schwabnetwork.com/articles)Top Economic Data to Watch Week of June 1, 2026. However, this week the focus shifts to economic data, earnings from several cybersecurity and semiconductor companies, and the [potential deal between the U.S. and Iran](https://schwabnetwork.com/video/geopolitics-and-oil-aarathi-krishnan-on-the-u-s-iran-disconnect). As May data trickle in, markets will focus on the direction of [inflation, the labor market, and key sentiment](https://schwabnetwork.com/video/looking-past-the-headlines-lance-mcgray-on-inflation-and-rates) indicators across major U.S. industries. On the economic data front, Monday kicks off the week with a look into the industrial economy via the ISM Manufacturing PMI. Two components within this report will be of key focus: the headline PMI number, which over the last several months has reflected improvement in the manufacturing industry among the purchasing managers surveyed, and the ISM Manufacturing Prices component. Consensus expectations call for ADP to come in at 110,000 jobs added for the month of May. The week closes with the BLS Employment Report, where the market is expecting Nonfarm Employment Change of 95,000 jobs added for the month and an unemployment rate of 4.3%.

Global Markets Enter a Data-Heavy Week (June 1 – 5, 2026): What Investors Should Watch. This week could prove crucial for global markets as investors navigate a packed economic calendar that will provide fresh clues on growth, inflation, and the future path of interest rates. For investors, the key question remains: Is the global economy cooling enough to justify policy easing, or resilient enough to keep rates higher for longer? Oil prices tumbled this week as hopes of a US-Iran agreement and a possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz eased supply concerns.
